title: The Feral Way of the Hunt
summary: How followers of the Road of the Beast are taught to kill.

claims.text: Ferals feel no remorse for their prey. A strike should be fast and hard, the hunt short, and the prey taken whole once brought down.
They hold that the Beast is not fed by half a kill or a few sips from a willing thrall; it wants the prey's life-blood, taken quickly and cleanly in the hunt.

title: Ferals and the Other Roads
summary: Why the Beast's followers distrust faith and philosophy.

claims.text: Ferals face the Beast directly rather than seeking answers from a God or Devil who plainly does not care.
They see the other roads as ways for Cainites to distract themselves from their true nature.
Because Ferals respect strength, powerful Cainites on other roads earn their regard, though they are thought impressive but misguided.

title: The Path of the Hunter
summary: Ferals who live by instinct and divide the world into hunters and prey.

claims.text: Followers explore the Beast's predatory side, set reason aside and let instinct guide them.
They split the world into hunters, fellow predators who deserve respect, and prey, who deserve only contempt.
Its ethics teach that the Beast exists to serve the hunt and should be mastered like a hunting animal.

title: The Road of the Slain
summary: The Via Einherjar of the northern Gangrel.

claims.text: Gangrel of the north follow the Road of the Slain, or Via Einherjar, which closely resembles the Road of the Beast.

title: Muslim Ferals of Iberia
summary: Brujah and Banu Haqim raiders of the taifa kingdoms.

claims.text: A band of Brujah and Banu Haqim, Muslim by birth and Ferals by choice, is spread across the taifa kingdoms of southern Iberia.
They say they only defend their lands, but they meet every few weeks to plan and carry out raids on their Christian enemies; other Ferals distrust them for clinging so closely to their faith.
